status: Fixed; broader staging suite has an independent error-code regression
finding: The git commit task-scoped staging regression deleted its fixed temporary repository immediately after Git/CLI work completed. On Windows, a short-lived file handle could make the final rmSync return EPERM, turning otherwise completed regression assertions into exit 1.
expectedBehavior: Fixture cleanup must remain bounded and retry transient Windows directory-lock errors, while preserving a real failure for persistent cleanup errors.
evidenceOrRepro: Reproduced 2026-09-02: `node --strip-types tests/cli/git-commit-task-scoped-staging.test.ts` reached final cleanup and threw `EPERM` on `.atm-temp-test-git-commit-task-scoped-staging`. The fixture now uses Node rmSync recursive retry semantics (10 retries, 100ms delay) both before setup and after assertions. The same test intentionally held a live branch queue lock for the default 15 seconds, which pushed the full Windows fixture beyond the terminal window. The commit timeout now also bounds branch-queue acquisition; the regression explicitly supplies `--timeout-ms 100`, receives `ATM_GIT_COMMIT_BRANCH_QUEUE_BUSY` with `queueLockTimeoutMs: 100`, and proceeds past that scenario. The complete fixture subsequently failed at a separate existing assertion: it expected `ATM_INDEX_FOREIGN_ACTIVE_STAGED` but received `ATM_PROTECTED_GOVERNANCE_STATE_DESTRUCTIVE_WRITE`; its final cleanup did not emit EPERM.
followUp: Investigate the separate protected-governance-state versus foreign-active-index error-code precedence before declaring the full staging suite green. Frozen runner publication and formal governance closeout remain separate from this quickfix.
